brief: Wave-0 entity predicate: bit 3 of the record flag byte, inverted.
decl: std::uint32_t entity_flag3(std::span<const std::byte> table, std::uint32_t index);
notes: Body: an empty or NULL table returns 1; otherwise return 1 when bit 3 of
table_base[index*28 + 0x1a] is clear and 0 when it is set. Sibling of
entity_flag (0x405df0), which tests bit 0 with normal polarity and no
NULL default; the two share the record layout but not the contract.
The host form models a missing table as an empty span.
Verified against the original by tools.w0_int_leaf_oracle.

bookkeeping.scope: Complete body. The inverted bit-3 predicate is matched across 12 oracle cases over two table bases, three indices and both polarities, plus the empty-table default.
bookkeeping.supported_domain: Indices whose 28-byte record lies inside the supplied table; an out-of-range index is rejected rather than emulated. An empty table models the original NULL base and returns one.
unresolved: What bit 3 means and which entity system owns the records.
bookkeeping.acceptance: Met: 9 fresh original-execution cases matched bit-exact by the native runner; self-test registered in ctest. See docs/recovery/cell-comparisons.md.
